messages.content:
Let \( a_0, a_1, a_2, \ldots \) be the unique sequence of nonnegative integers less than 397 with \( a_0 = 1 \) and

\[ a_{n+1}(a_n + 1)^2 \equiv a_n \pmod{397} \]

for all nonnegative integers \( n \). Given that \( a_{2026} = 9 \), compute the remainder when \( a_0 + a_1 + \cdots + a_{2026} \) is divided by 397.

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

message.content:
Work modulo \(397\). Since \(397\) is prime and the sequence is defined for all \(n\), the terms involved are invertible modulo \(397\).

Given

\[
a_{n+1}(a_n+1)^2 \equiv a_n \pmod{397},
\]

divide by \(a_n a_{n+1}\) to get

\[
\frac{(a_n+1)^2}{a_n}\equiv \frac1{a_{n+1}}.
\]

Thus

\[
a_n+2+\frac1{a_n}\equiv \frac1{a_{n+1}},
\]

so

\[
a_n \equiv \frac1{a_{n+1}}-\frac1{a_n}-2.
\]

Summing from \(n=0\) to \(2026\),

\[
\sum_{n=0}^{2026} a_n
\equiv \frac1{a_{2027}}-\frac1{a_0}-2\cdot 2027.
\]

We are given \(a_{2026}=9\), so

\[
a_{2027}\cdot 10^2 \equiv 9 \pmod{397}.
\]

Since \(100^{-1}\equiv 266\pmod{397}\),

\[
a_{2027}\equiv 9\cdot 266\equiv 12 \pmod{397}.
\]

Therefore

\[
\frac1{a_{2027}}\equiv \frac1{12}\equiv 364 \pmod{397},
\]

and \(a_0=1\), so

\[
\sum_{n=0}^{2026} a_n
\equiv 364-1-2\cdot 2027.
\]

Now \(2\cdot 2027\equiv 84\pmod{397}\), hence

\[
\sum_{n=0}^{2026} a_n
\equiv 364-1-84=279 \pmod{397}.
\]

\[
\boxed{279}
\]
